## Independent Sonnet Review — `codex/cb-keyword-final` (8400976796ab)

**Source SHA:** `8400976796ab1c1ee7a783769b3164fee186e441`  
**Base:** `57f6b324bfd30a18c5e9f79541dd62e48ec38e0b`

---

### Production change — `src/utils/keyword-match.ts`

**Semantic equivalence with original regex.** The original `^[^a-z0-9]+|[^a-z0-9]+$` accepts only ASCII digits and lowercase letters at token boundaries. `isAsciiLetterOrDigit` accepts exactly `[48,57]∪[97,122]` — the same set. No upper-case, no non-ASCII.

**UTF-16 boundary handling.** The forward scan calls `codePointAt(start)` and advances `start++` unconditionally. For a valid surrogate pair at positions *n, n+1*: position *n* returns the full code point (> 122, fails), `start++`; position *n+1* returns the low-surrogate value (~56320, fails), `start++`. Both units are consumed, identical to the original regex without the `u` flag treating surrogates as individual characters. The backward scan `codePointAt(end-1)` on the low-surrogate position returns the low-surrogate scalar (not the composed code point), also > 122, also rejected — symmetric. Lone surrogates are rejected the same way.

**`codePointAt` can never return `undefined` inside the loop bodies.** `start < end ≤ raw.length` guarantees `start < raw.length`; `end > start ≥ 0` guarantees `end-1 ≥ 0 < raw.length`. The `?? -1` guard is unreachable but harmless.

**Performance claim is verified by differential data.** 2k/4k/8k times of 6/24/96 ms (≈ 4× per 2× input = quadratic) on the original; 100k/200k/400k times of 0.11/0.29/0.49 ms (linear) on the new code. The `A + !×200k + B` test enforces a 4-second budget *after* a confirmed READY signal, with separate 15-second startup budget — the timer hand-off is correct and cannot mask import latency as work time.

**`words` Set insertion order** is preserved: `ordered` is unaffected (only `cleaned` is pushed); sub-token decomposition (`split(/[^a-z0-9]+/)`) is unchanged. The differential oracle verifies `[...words]` ordering across 5,010 fixtures.

### Test additions — `geo-keyword-matching.test.mts`

**UTF-16/surrogate fixture correctness (manually verified):**

- `['!!!A---B???', ['a---b'], ['a---b','a','b']]` — trim strips leading `!!!` and trailing `???`, internal `---` retained ✓  
- `['😀A😀B😀', ['a😀b'], ...]` — both surrogate units rejected at both ends, `a😀b` retained ✓  
- `['\ud800A\udc00', ['a'], ['a']]` — lone surrogates stripped at each end ✓  
- `['\ud800\udc00', [], []]` — no ASCII interior, empty result ✓  
- `['A---B a---b\u00a0C', ['a---b','a---b','c'], ['a---b','a','b','c']]` — `\u00a0` is in `\s`, splits correctly; Set deduplication preserves insertion order ✓  
- `['０1２', ['1'], ['1']]` — fullwidth digits are non-ASCII (> 122), only the ASCII `1` survives ✓

**Child process handshake.** `stdout` is accumulated before the `includes('READY\n')` check, so a READY split across chunks is handled. Timer is cleared before arming the work timer; closed event always clears the active timer. No leak path.

**Selector test.** Imports the real `targeted-tests.mjs` exports (not a mock). Verifies exact command string, `deriveScriptIndex` acceptance, both changed-file paths routing to `test:keyword-match`, and `commandToStages` output for `node --test --import tsx ...`. All three assertions match the provided selector source.
